title: Algorithms & Data Structures: Foundations
welcome_lead: Map the core building blocks — arrays, stacks, queues and linked lists.
meta_desc: A-Level Computer Science: linear data structures, ADTs, and basic operations.
final_note: Master these primitives — every advanced algorithm rests on them.

concepts.def: A fixed-size contiguous sequence of elements indexed from 0.
A LIFO abstract data type with push and pop operations.
A FIFO abstract data type with enqueue and dequeue operations.
A sequence of nodes where each node holds data and a pointer to the next.
A model defined by behaviour, not by implementation.
A variable that stores the memory address of another value.

walkthroughs.body_html: An array stores elements in contiguous memory — random access is O(1) but insertion in the middle is O(n). A linked list stores nodes anywhere in memory, joined by pointers — insertion at the head is O(1) but indexed access is O(n).

A stack is last-in-first-out: think of plates. Push adds to the top, pop removes from the top. A queue is first-in-first-out: think of a line. Enqueue adds to the rear, dequeue removes from the front.
An abstract data type specifies what operations exist (push, pop) without saying how they are implemented. A stack can be built on an array or a linked list — the client code does not need to know.
